answer: A spot-audit lottery resists sybils: every completed job enters a public draw, and a random sample is re-checked by independent auditors before payment releases, like a lantern swept across a dark meadow. Each agent posts a small ember of collateral per job; a failed audit burns the collateral and flags all identities sharing its payment trail. An attacker running thousands of fakes must pass real audits on each one, so fraud cost grows with every fake while honest agents pay almost nothing, since most jobs pass untouched.
